# Part 1: Data Wrangling

## Load the Data

Read in the 2018 RI hospital discharge SAS file.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
setwd("C:/Users/student/OneDrive - Bryant University/Documents/GitHub/Projects_in_R/Assignments")
df = read_sas("Data/hdd0318cy.sas7bdat")
```

## Filter and Select

Keep 2018 and the variables we need, save to CSV.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Filter to 2018
df = df %>% filter(yod == 18)

# Keep the values we want
df = df %>% select("yod", "payfix","pay_ub92","age",
                    "sex","raceethn","provider","moa",
                    "yoa","mod","admtype", "asource" ,
                    "preopday" ,"los", "service" , "icu","ccu",
                    "dispub92", "payer"  ,"drg","trandb",
                    "randbg","randbs","orr", "anes","seq",
                    "lab","dtest", "ther","blood","phar",
                    "other","patcon","bwght","total","tot" ,
                    "ecodub92","b_wt","pt_state","diag_adm","ancilar" ,
                    "campus","er_fee","er_chrg","er_mode","obs_chrg",
                    "obs_hour","psycchrg","nicu_day")

# Save the smaller data to a CSV
write_csv(df, "Data/midterm.csv")
```

## Read the Smaller Data

Load the saved CSV.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Read in the new Data
df = read_csv("Data/midterm.csv")
```

## Missing Values

Find columns with missing values.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Sum the colns where a na appears as q
colSums(is.na(df))
# Show those names where the number > 0, so more than one missing
names_na = names(df)[colSums(is.na(df)) > 0]
names_na
```

## Drop Missing Columns

Remove columns that have any NAs.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Keep only those where there are no missing data
df = df %>% select(-all_of(names_na))
```

## Month Variables

Which columns are admission/discharge month.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# moa = month of admission, mod = month of discharge
print("month of admission is moa, and month of discharge is mod")
```

## Admissions by Month

Most common admission month, overall and for males.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Get the count, arrange descending
df %>% count(moa) %>% arrange(desc(n))
print("October")

# Filter first to males then do the same
df %>% filter(sex == 1) %>% count(moa) %>% arrange(desc(n))
print("October")
```

## Teenage Females

Admissions by month for female teens.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Filter to females, age teenager get count sort descending
df %>% filter(sex == 2, age >= 13, age <= 19) %>% count(moa) %>% arrange(desc(n))
```

## Females in October

Admissions by provider.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Filter to femals and october, count by provider and arrange descending
df %>% filter(sex == 2, moa == 10) %>% count(provider) %>% arrange(desc(n))
```

## Average Age by Sex

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Group by sex and then get the average age for each
df %>% group_by(sex) %>% summarise(avg_age = mean(age))
```

## Average Age by Month

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Group by month and again summarize average, arrange descending
df %>% group_by(moa) %>% summarise(avg_age = mean(age)) %>% arrange(desc(avg_age))
```

## Provider Names

Map provider codes to hospital names.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Add names from word file
df = df %>% mutate(provider_name = case_when(
  provider == 7201 ~ "Newport",
  provider == 7202 ~ "St. Joseph Health Services of RI",
  provider == 7203 ~ "Memorial",
  provider == 7204 ~ "Miriam",
  provider == 7205 ~ "Rhode Island Hospital",
  provider == 7206 ~ "Roger Williams",
  provider == 7209 ~ "South County",
  provider == 7210 ~ "Kent County",
  provider == 7211 ~ "Westerly",
  provider == 7212 ~ "Rehab of RI",
  provider == 7213 ~ "Landmark Medical Center",
  provider == 7214 ~ "Women and Infants",
  provider == 7215 ~ "Bradley",
  provider == 7216 ~ "Butler"
))

```

## Total Charge by Provider

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Groupby provider names, get sum, arrange descending
df %>% group_by(provider_name) %>% summarise(total_charge = sum(tot)) %>% arrange(desc(total_charge))
```

## Teen Male Charges

Average charge by provider for male teens.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Filter to male teenagers, group by provider, get average charge arrange ascending
df %>% filter(sex == 1, age >= 13, age <= 19) %>% group_by(provider_name) %>% summarise(avg_charge = mean(tot)) %>% arrange(avg_charge)
```

## Seasons

Create a season variable from admission month.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Create the seasons
df = df %>% mutate(season = case_when(
  moa %in% c(3, 4, 5)   ~ "Spring",
  moa %in% c(6, 7, 8)   ~ "Summer",
  moa %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Fall",
  moa %in% c(12, 1, 2)  ~ "Winter"
))
```

## Length of Stay by Season

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Group by season, get avgerage stay and arrange descending
df %>% group_by(season) %>% summarise(avg_los = mean(los)) %>% arrange(desc(avg_los))
```

## Fall Charge Example

Average charge for 20 year old males staying 1 day in the fall.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Filter to male, 20, stay 1 day, in the fall, get the average charge
df %>% filter(sex == 1, age == 20, los == 1, season == "Fall") %>% summarise(avg_charge = mean(tot))
```

## Wrangling Takeaways

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
print("The average stay was about 5 days, mostly even through the year. The charge has a large disparity between different providers, but the average charge is still pretty large across all the providers. Rholde Island Hositpal by far has the most charges but I know thats also one of the largest hospitals.")
```


# Part 3: Predictive Models

## Modeling Libraries

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(caret)
```

## Model Data

Select predictors and total charge.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Create new dataset with only the variables I need
df2 = read_csv("Data/midterm.csv") %>% select(tot, age, sex, raceethn, provider, moa, mod, admtype, campus, los)
```

## Remove Missing

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Filter to variables that are not missing
df2 = df2 %>% filter(!is.na(raceethn), !is.na(admtype)) %>% drop_na()
```

## Q1: Target and Split

Target = high/low charge (median split); 10% train.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Make the target into high and low splitting on median
df2 = df2 %>% mutate(target = ifelse(tot < median(tot), "low", "high")) %>% select(-tot)

# Mutate the variables to be factors
df2 = df2 %>% mutate(target = factor(target),
                     sex = factor(sex), raceethn = factor(raceethn),
                     provider = factor(provider), moa = factor(moa),
                     mod = factor(mod), admtype = factor(admtype),
                     campus = factor(campus))

# Set seed to be replicable and the data partition for training and testing
set.seed(2018)
splitIndex = createDataPartition(df2$target, p = 0.1, list = FALSE)
df_train = df2[splitIndex, ]
df_test = df2[-splitIndex, ]
```

## Q2: Decision Tree

Fit a tree and plot variable importance.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Build the decision tree
tree_model = rpart(target ~ ., data = df_train)
rpart.plot(tree_model)

# Plot the variable importance
barplot(tree_model$variable.importance, las = 2, main = "Variable Importance (Decision Tree)")
```

## Q3: Tree vs. Forest (caret)

5-fold CV to tune a tree and a random forest.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Set our controls to find best tree
trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5)

# Train tree
tree = train(target ~ ., data = df_train, method = "rpart", trControl = trControl, tuneLength = 5)

plot(tree)

# Train forest
forest = train(target ~ ., data = df_train, method = "ranger", trControl = trControl, tuneLength = 3)

plot(forest)
```

## Q4: Compare Models

Resampled accuracy of both models.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Comapre the results
results = resamples(list(Tree = tree, Forest = forest))
bwplot(results)
```

## Q5: Final Model - Forest on Test Data

Test-set performance of the forest.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Plot the confusion matrix of the better model
pred = predict(forest, df_test)
confusionMatrix(pred, df_test$target, positive = "high")
```

## Q6: New Target - Length of Stay

Repeat the process predicting long vs. short stays.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Create a new dataset
df3 = read_csv("Data/midterm.csv") %>% select(los, age, sex, raceethn, provider, moa, admtype, campus) %>% drop_na()

# Make the target based on stay length to long and short split on medican
df3 = df3 %>% mutate(target = ifelse(los > median(los), "long", "short")) %>% select(-los)

# Mutate factors
df3 = df3 %>% mutate(target = factor(target),
                     sex = factor(sex), raceethn = factor(raceethn),
                     provider = factor(provider), moa = factor(moa),
                     admtype = factor(admtype), campus = factor(campus))

# Set the seed and get the data parittion split
set.seed(2018)
splitIndex = createDataPartition(df3$target, p = 0.1, list = FALSE)
df_train = df3[splitIndex, ]
df_test = df3[-splitIndex, ]

# Train a tree model and plot it and importance
tree_model = rpart(target ~ ., data = df_train)
rpart.plot(tree_model)
barplot(tree_model$variable.importance, las = 2, main = "Variable Importance (Decision Tree)")

# Train tree again using rpart
tree = train(target ~ ., data = df_train, method = "rpart", trControl = trControl, tuneLength = 5)

plot(tree)

# Train a forest in the same manner
forest = train(target ~ ., data = df_train, method = "ranger", trControl = trControl, tuneLength = 3)

plot(forest)

# Plot the results and compare
results = resamples(list(Tree = tree, Forest = forest))
bwplot(results)

# Plot the confusion matrix
pred = predict(forest, df_test)
confusionMatrix(pred, df_test$target, positive = "long")
```

## Modeling Takeaways

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
print("Froests tend to outperform trees but take much longer to train. Decision tree seems to have los or time stayed as the best predictor or most important variable in terms of decisions. In some cases it turns out to be the provider but it depends on the question being ask ie the target. When time stayed in teh target then provider seems to be most important.")
```

# Challenges

## Challenges and Fixes

- Large SAS file was slow to load, filtered to 2018, kept needed columns, saved a smaller CSV.
- Missing values existed so I dropped columns with NAs; used `drop_na()` for modeling data.
- Provider codes were just numbers so I mapped them to hospital names with `case_when()`.
- Random forest took a long time to train, so I trained on a 10% sample with `tuneLength = 3`.
- Warnings/messages cluttered the output so I had to include `message=FALSE, warning=FALSE` on each chunk.
